UpCloud.summary_note: UpCloud is a compelling EU sovereignty story: a Finnish privately held company backed exclusively by EU investors (Finnish state fund Tesi, Finnish VC Inventure, Dutch Connected Capital), with a detailed and proactive published legal analysis confirming the US CLOUD Act does not apply to EU customer data. Its EU Access Management Policy — restricting privileged EU data center access to EU employees only — is among the most explicitly documented of any EU IaaS provider. The subprocessor model is exceptionally clean: for EU virtual server services, UpCloud uses zero third-party subprocessors. Key weaknesses relative to larger EU providers are: no BSI C5 attestation (German gold standard); no customer-managed encryption key (BYOK/KMS) product; ESG reporting is early-stage (first report in 2024) with limited specific metrics; only 70% of data centers run on renewable energy; and as a smaller provider (~83–130 employees), service breadth is narrower than STACKIT, OVHcloud, or T Cloud Public. The legal sovereignty architecture (CLOUD Act analysis, Finnish jurisdiction, EU-only investors, EU-only infrastructure access) is a genuine strength that directly addresses the primary concern of EU public sector and regulated-industry customers.
